newsitem.title: ITALY: Autostrade sale may be delayed - IMI.
newsitem.headline: Autostrade sale may be delayed - IMI.

text.p: The sale of Italy's main motorway operator, Autostrade Spa, may have to be delayed because parliament has imposed tough conditions on the sale, the head of one of the banks handling the operation said on Tuesday.
Italy has promised to privatise Autostrade, which is controlled by state holding IRI, before the end of June in order to comply with a European Commission ruling on the reduction of IRI debts.

But a parliamentary committee last month ordered the creation of a stable core of shareholders to take 20-25 percent of the firm's capital. These shareholders must pledge not to sell their stake for at least three years.
"The parliamentary committee has imposed demands that will be hard to overcome in the short-term," said Rainer Masera, the director general of bank IMI.
IMI and Schroeder have been appointed as advisers for the Autostrade sell-off.
Autostrade controls around 3,000 kilometres of motorway throughout Italy.
